title: 60-Year-Old Man Found Dead In Tamil Nadu Jail, Suicide Suspected | Chennai-news News - News18
text:
Body of a 60-year-old man was found hanging inside a police station in Tamil Nadu’s Coimbatore. As per the police, suicide is suspected. The man was found dead in the sub-inspector’s room on the first floor of the police station at B1 Bazar Police Station on Tuesday night. As per the police, the man with intellectual disability allegedly committed suicide after locking SI’s room. Police personnel on duty was unaware of his intentions.
Recommended Stories A report by Hindustan Times cited Coimbatore City Police Commissioner A Saravana Sundar who stated that the deceased was unmarried and was living with his sister and elderly mother. His sister allegedly mentioned that the man has been behaving unusually over the past two days and he feels like someone would kill him.
Sundar further said the man sneaked into the police station on Tuesday and hanged himself from the ceiling fan.
Meanwhile, BJP has raised suspicion over the suicide. Party’s state president Nainar Nagenthiran targeted MK Stalin led Tamil Nadu government and threatened to stage a protest against “corrupt police force."
BJP Questions TN Government
Raising suspicion over the suicide, Nagenthiran asked the government, “Therefore, how did no one notice that the person who came to file a complaint was at the police station all night? Did the person who came to file a complaint bring a noose to the police station? Did none of the police officers notice it? More importantly, isn’t it standard procedure to obtain the full address of the person filing a complaint?"
He went ahead and asked CM MK Stalin to answer his questions and posted, “In that case, what is the police trying to cover up by saying they don’t even know who the deceased is? How was someone whose identity is unknown allowed access to the assistant inspector’s room? Didn’t anyone even pass by the assistant inspector’s room for cleaning until 10 a.m.? Was the person perhaps beaten to death under the guise of an investigation? It is the duty of the Chief Minister, Mr. @mkstalin, to answer all these questions."
